action: owner-directed synchronization simplification and weak-reference review
authorization: User accepted missed object disposal for additions racing with bin disposal and requested avoiding unnecessary synchronization in ObjectsBin/SharedObjectsBin while reviewing WeakReferenceSet.
contract: Object disposal for in-flight additions is best effort. Storage handle ownership must remain safe under concurrent Add, TryTake, compaction and disposal.

findings.problem: An addition could pass the open check, pause through final queue draining, then publish a handle after the cleaner handle had been freed and finalization suppressed.
findings.resolution: Hold the existing read lock through allocation/reuse and queue publication; hold the write lock through closure and both drains.

findings.problem: A handle removed from a queue could be recycled after concurrent disposal had already drained the queues. Previous partial lock scopes did not protect the whole ownership transfer.
findings.resolution: Protect retrieval and recycling as one read-locked operation, and complete compaction/disposal as write-locked operations.

findings.problem: Compaction could process and republish handles across disposal; cleaner lifetime documentation also incorrectly denied its strong owner reference.
findings.resolution: Check closed state under the write lock before processing or scheduling a new cleaner; correct reference-direction comments.

simplifications: Remove ObjectsBin._syncRoot and the outer addition/disposal gate.
Retain only Interlocked.Exchange to claim bin storage once; ordinary additions capture the storage directly.
Replace SharedObjectsBin CAS/Volatile loop with Interlocked.Increment; retain atomic decrement.
Keep the existing ServiceProvider live-parent acquisition gate, which already prevents shared-count resurrection.
Remove WeakReferenceSet.TryDequeueSafe; retrieval now owns its read lock for the complete handle operation.
limitations: No performance improvement claimed or benchmark run. Add/TryTake now take the existing storage read lock; compaction holds the write lock for its complete pass and can delay operations on large sets.
A racing bin addition may be rejected without disposing its supplied object, or may be accepted after the object-drain pass; this is explicitly accepted by the owner.
The reader/writer lock is intentionally not disposed while pending cleaner finalizers may still enter it.
Concurrency stress covers interleavings but is not an exhaustive scheduler proof; lock-scope ownership was also reviewed directly.

verification.git_diff_check: Passed; Git reported only an existing LF/CRLF normalization notice.

coverage: Compaction after disposal cannot recreate cleaner/resources.
Concurrent compaction/retrieval preserves every strongly reachable entry exactly once.
Concurrent add/take/compaction/repeated disposal leave both handle queues empty and the cleaner handle unallocated.
Existing bin, failure cleanup, ownership and scope acquisition tests remain green.
Racing bin addition test now asserts no double disposal and permits zero disposal calls under the revised contract.
prior_evidence: IMPLEMENTATION.P1.json remains a historical result; its original strong bin-addition policy and source fingerprints are superseded here.
